headline: Noah compares the three experiments and reaches their actual calibration, clap-detection, and game surfaces on the local build.
overview: A live product-level walk for Breath Quest, framed around Noah Bennett's actual decision rather than a list of routes.
payoff: Noah compares the three experiments and reaches their actual calibration, clap-detection, and game surfaces on the local build.

scenes.title: The project is explicit about being an experiment
scenes.narrative: Three hypotheses separate breath detection, clap patterns, and a playful sound-controlled runner instead of pretending one sensor already solves everything.
frameCaptions: The project is explicit about being an experiment
scenes.action: Opened the local Breath Quest build.

scenes.title: Breath control begins with calibration
scenes.narrative: The real interface explains that personal microphone levels must be calibrated before gameplay; the dependency is visible, not hidden.

scenes.title: Clap detection exposes its live controls
scenes.narrative: Start/stop listening, detection counts, settings, timelines, and play feedback expose what the recognizer is doing.
frameCaptions: Clap detection exposes its live controls

scenes.title: The signal is tested in an actual game
scenes.narrative: The third hypothesis moves beyond meters into onboarding, lives, scoring, and a complete game loop controlled by sound.
frameCaptions: The signal is tested in an actual game

scenes.title: The sensor can be inspected, not merely trusted
scenes.narrative: Time-domain, frequency, envelope, and zero-crossing tools make the experimental signal visible to Noah before he treats it as a controller.
frameCaptions: The sensor can be inspected, not merely trusted
